newsitem.title: USA: Florida says key tobacco lawsuit points intact.
newsitem.headline: Florida says key tobacco lawsuit points intact.

text.p: Florida Governor Lawton Chiles said on Tuesday that a judge's ruling dismissing all but three counts of the state's Medicaid lawsuit against the tobacco industry had left the most important parts of the suit intact.
"The court has pared down the suit," Chiles told reporters.
"The good news for us is that we're left with our count of negligence and strict liability. We're also left with our count for injunctive relief to stop the targeting of our kids."
Philip Morris Cos Inc hailed the ruling by Harold Cohen, a circuit judge in West Palm Beach, as a victory for the industry.
Chiles disagreed. "They always do (claim victory)," he said. "I just wonder what they're going to say when the verdict is in."
He said the state had lost in Cohen's ruling what it had expected to lose.

Among other things, Cohen barred Florida from seeking reimbursement from the tobacco industry for smoking-related Medicaid expenses incurred before 1994, when a law was passed allowing the state to seek such reimbursement.
Cohen also ordered a second round of mediation between the state and the tobacco industry.

"We're willing to mediate," Chiles said. "We have been to start with. The court has determined we have three good counts of negligence and strict liability. It may be that (tobacco companies) will know they are facing trial and they'll seek to mediate. We look forward to trying."
A July attempt to reach an out-of-court settlement ended quickly without an agreement.
Florida officials hope to recoup more than $400 million a year in Medicaid payments for tobacco-related illnesses since 1994.
Florida is suing the tobacco industry under a 1994 state law that strips cigarette makers of most of their traditional defenses in a liability lawsuit.
